l: The Chief of Police has the ultimate authority and responsibility for the fiscal management of the department. As the Chief of Police's designee, the Assistant Chief over the Finance and Personnel Bureau will oversee the financial administration responsibilities for final budget preparation and fiscal management functions for the department. TBP 1.02

A. The Finance and Personnel Bureau will have six (6) areas of responsibility: Police Administration, Fiscal Command, Personnel/Program Support Command, Operational Command, Community Alliance Command, and Police Chaplain.
1. Police Chaplain - responsible for providing counseling and assistance to any employee or their family; officiating at police funerals; and monitoring of personnel on extended sick leave.
Police Administration consists of the Office of the Chief of Police and the Public Relations Office.
A. The Administrative Sergeant is responsible for:

1. Assisting with the administrative responsibilities of the Chief of Police; approving, at the direction of the Chief of Police and/or Executive Command Staff, any request for department participation in a training event, public event, presentation, assessment center, or any other participation requested of the department, with the exception of normal divisional and intervention related events.

2. Liaison with the police associations in matters concerning the police department, specifically with the Fort Worth Police Officers Association (FWPOA) concerning the Meet and Confer Labor Agreement between City of Fort Worth and Fort Worth Police Officers Association. The President of the FWPOA is assigned to the Police Administration Office.
B. The Public Relations Office Sergeant is responsible for: TBP 5.04

1. Responding to requests in relation to public information from citizens and/or the media; coordinates activities related to press releases, press conferences, and media events involving the police department; and coordinates community forums, town hall meetings, and other public events initiated by the Public Relations Office.
2. Public Information Officer(s) shall serve as official spokesperson(s) for the department in the release of information to department personnel, the public, and to media outlets.

The Fiscal Command shall be the responsibility of a Police Assistant Director and has responsibility to manage budget planning and management, finance, grants, procurement, contract management, and Crime Control and Prevention District budget. The Fiscal Command is responsible for the Budget and Procurement Division and the Finance Division. The Fiscal Command Assistant Director is the Budget Director for the Crime Control and Prevention District Fund. TBP 1.03

1. Budget Section - develop and manage the Police Department’s annual general fund operating budgets and 5-year CIP plan; manage fiscal administration of general fund capital projects; oversee the Police Department Budget Committee; and submit General Fund forecast of funds.

2. Procurement Section - process vouchers and all Travel and Training forms process accounts receivable and other revenue received by the department; manage the procurement process including requisitions and purchase orders.

a. Asset Management Unit - responsible for the centralization of issuing, receiving, processing, inventorying, and monitoring of all fixed assets and all other department assets, owned or donated for the Police Department; and coordinating the annual validation and inventory of those assets.

b. Contract Management Section - responsible for managing, supporting and administering the contract process including developing, negotiating and executing contracts in support of the Police Department.

B. Finance Division – conduct internal audits of a financial nature to confirm department compliance; reconcile all grant overtime and personnel-related costs to ensure compliance with all directives.

1. Financial Compliance Unit – ensure compliance of supplemental funds and expenditures and research proposed asset forfeiture purchases to confirm permissibility with directives; oversee Imprest funds for each unit to ensure compliance with Federal and State guidelines; and research proposed asset forfeiture purchases to confirm permissibility with State and Federal guidelines. TBP 7.12
2. Crime Control and Prevention District (CCPD) Unit – develop, coordinate, and manage the police department’s annual Crime Control and Prevention District (CCPD) operating and capital budgets.
3. Supplemental Funding Section - responsible for researching, developing, managing, and submitting all grant applications and managing asset forfeiture, donations, and task forces.
The Personnel/Program Support Command shall be the responsibility of a Police Assistant Director and has responsibility to manage Employment Services, Program Support, and the Police Payroll.

1. Employment Services Unit - maintain department personnel files, including performance reviews and officer efficiencies; facilitate department out-processing paperwork; setup and/or remove assignment pays; ensure employment-related compliance with department, city, state and federal employment policies; and provide employment-related training as necessary.

a. Civil service - Request promotional exams, certified lists and process promotions, military overages and demotions; responsible for the Civil Service G Files; provide unit information to the Civil Service Director for maintenance of A File; assist with updating or initiating employment ordinances and policies, and manage staffing projections for attrition.

b. Civilian - facilitate civilian hiring, to include job postings, interviews, conditional offers of employment and background screening process; participate in the employment selection and process of civilian police personnel; and assist in employee relations issues and provide guidance in discipline and termination procedures.

2. Position Management Unit - responsible for coordinating all personnel moves, pay, hire and termination; monitoring position alignment; and producing the Personnel Orders; processing and monitoring military leaves for sworn and civilian employees participating in military training and/or deployment; and entering staffing and benefits for annual budget preparation.

3. Medical Records Unit - responsible for compliance with all procedures, policies and filing related to occupational and non-occupational illnesses, Major Medical Sick Leave, Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA), limited duty, and voluntary leave.

4. Polygraph Examiner Detail - administers employment polygraph examinations for department applicants when requested by Employment Services or the Training Academy, a supervisor or detective; and, when requested by the Chief of Police, administers polygraph examination to any departmental employee. TBP 4.04

1. The Research and Planning Section is responsible for strategic planning; serving as a liaison to the Property Management Department in coordinating and implementing facility capital improvement projects; overseeing and tracking data and measures used for operational decisions; research projects; reporting crime statistics to the public; updating the department’s website; developing departmental reports and plans; providing departmental Geographic Information System services; and providing support to the Crime Control and Prevention District Board of Directors.

2. Technology Services is responsible for researching and project management of technology advancements; application development and support; user support; master data management; capital project planning; budget planning of technology related assets and services; assisting with and supporting technology-related facility improvements and hardware moves; and ensuring compliance with technology-related federal, state and local regulations and policies including CJIS, HIPPA, Privacy Policy, etc.

Responsible for payroll related function and work activities to ensure timesheet entries, work quality and adherence to established policies and procedures. Ensure city payroll processes and activities meet audit requirements and participates in regular audits for data verification purposes; supports employees and management by providing interpretation and advice on general payroll related issues; and provides data to employees, management and Police Command staff as needed and acts as liaison to other city departments regarding ERP and paycheck issues.

The Operational Command shall be the responsibility of a Deputy Chief and shall include Professional Standards, Training Division, Fleet Services Division, Use of Force Analysis Section, Policy Management and Safety Section, and Ceremonial Unit.

1. Special Investigations Unit – responsibilities include conducting administrative audits and/or inspections of police department operations to ensure the goals and objectives of the City of Fort Worth, as it pertains to public safety, are being met in an efficient and effective manner; audit and inspections conducted at the direction of the Chief of Police; and the investigation of criminal allegations involving a person employed by the City of Fort Worth, i.e., Police, Fire, Water, etc. that meet the following criteria:
a. Class B Misdemeanor offenses and above with exception to misdemeanor Driving While Intoxicated or Driving Under the Influence offenses.
b. Any allegation involving a criminal offense, regardless of classification, or family violence.
c. Criminal allegations involving City of Fort Worth employees if it is directly related to public integrity.

2. Internal Affairs Section - responsibilities include ensuring the complete and impartial investigation of all complaints against police department employees; maintaining records of investigations of allegations of misconduct and any action taken as a result of the investigation; conducting administrative investigations on Critical Police Incidents at the direction of the chain of command; and conducting investigations affecting department personnel at the direction of the Chief of Police.

a. Legal Liaison Unit - assist the Department of Law with document collection related to requests for police records; process legal requests to include expunctions, open records requests, subpoenas, disciplinary hearings, lawsuits, and court orders.

b. Court Liaison Detail - provide assistance to the Municipal Court and Tarrant County District Attorney's Office in the notification to police personnel of scheduled court appearances, subpoenas, and other court-related activities.

B. Training Division - responsibilities include developing, evaluating, and supervising all in-service training programs for members of the department and maintaining records of such training; developing, evaluating, and providing recruit and entry level training for all sworn job classifications in the department; coordinating state licensing and higher education as required by the Firefighters’ and Police Officers’ Civil Service Commission and the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement (TCOLE); responsibility for the Weapons Range; and coordinating all aspects of background investigations, hiring, coordinating all aspects of recruitment for cadets, explorers, interns and police applicants; and, coordinating the department’s Explorer Program.
1. Career Development – includes recruit training and advanced training.
2. Enhanced Skills – includes weapons training and reality-based training.

4. Reserve Officers Program – the primary function of Reserve Officers is to provide auxiliary staffing to the police department. Reserve Officers serve at the discretion of the Chief of Police and may be called into service at any time the Chief of Police or designee considers it necessary to have additional officers.

C. Fleet Services – responsibilities include managing the annual purchase of fleet vehicles and establishing vehicle specifications addressing the specific needs of the department’s specialized units; administering the police department’s vehicle lease program; providing management and accountability of the fleet’s maintenance and fuel expenditure; and, maintaining the appropriate database to ensure accountability of designated equipment.

D. Policy Management and Safety Section - responsible for assisting the command staff with policy decisions; development of the General Orders and Special Orders; maintaining the document management system (PowerDMS), assuring compliance of policies and procedures with applicable entities; program management and monitoring for the Texas Police Chief’s Best Practices Program; monitoring the police department website email; coordinating the department health and safety program; developing facility safety plans and employee safety courses; and performing safety inspections of all police facilities. TBP 1.13

1. Use of Force Coordinator – the primary mission of the Use of Force Coordinator is to reduce unnecessary use of force incidents, work toward increasing trust and legitimacy, and improve safety by concentrating on three key areas as they related to use of force: policy development, training, and increased transparency and community engagement. The Use of Force Coordinator shall serve as the chairperson of the Fort Worth Police Department Use of Force Review Board.

2. Force Analysis Section – provides a consistent review process for all Use of Force incidents, excluding Critical Police Incidents. The Force Analysis Section works closely with the Use of Force Review Board and the Training Academy to analyze these incidents and determine findings.

F. Ceremonial Unit – under the supervision of an appointee by the Operational Command Deputy Chief and consisting of the Honor Guard and the Pipes and Drums who provide traditional military and police honors at ceremonies and funerals of fallen police officers and dignitaries.
The Community Alliance Command shall be the responsibility of a Deputy Chief and shall include the Support Services Division, the Community Alliance Division, and the Wellness Unit.
A. The Support Services Division is responsible for providing general support services for the department, crime prevention, and interaction with the community.
1. Adult Community Program Section - provide coordination and training for: TBP 2.24

c. Police/Clergy Program - a community-focused initiative that brings together local clergy and members of the Fort Worth Police Department to collaboratively serve the residents of Fort Worth. The program also fosters trust, unity, and collaboration between law enforcement and local clergy and faith-based communities.

(1) At the heart of the initiative is the Police and Clergy Coalition (P.A.C.C.), a city-wide alliance of clergy members working together with police officers to promote public safety and community wellness, provide spiritual and emotional support during crises, build trust and legitimacy between the community and law enforcement, and engage in proactive community outreach and events.

(2) The Ministers Academy is a training platform designed to equip clergy with the tools and knowledge to effectively partner with police, understand law enforcement protocols, and enhance their roles as community leaders and peacebuilders.

d. Community Engagement Unit - employs community relationship strategies to strengthen trust between the community and the Fort Worth Police Department. The development of long-term relationships and community partnering leads to decreased crime and improved community perception of safety.
1. Crime Free Multi-Housing- works with other entities to educate and partner with multi-family dwellings to prevent and deter criminal activity.
2. Youth Program Section - provide coordination and training for: TBP 2.24

a. Fort Worth Police Department Cadet Program – responsible for recruitment, selection, processing, and monitoring of the cadets that are career-oriented toward seeking entrance to the police academy.
b. Police Athletic League – a collaboration between police and the community providing guidance and leadership to our youth through athletics.
c. Explorers - a career educational and experience-based program designed to help young people by focusing on character development, physical training and career education.
B. Community Alliance Division programs include:

a. Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) - responsible for reducing the hazards associated with interactions between law enforcement and people suffering from mental illness as well as proactively engaging mental health consumers who pose a threat to the community as a whole.

b. Homeless Outreach Program Enforcement (HOPE) – responsible for building a rapport within the homeless community, maintaining a positive police impact by way of service connections, and instilling a sense of self-worth in those considered chronically homeless.

c. Civilian Response Unit – Civilian Response Specialists are responsible for answering calls-for-service and performing tasks that do not require police officers’ presence, authority, or action and assisting the Patrol Bureau in any reasonable way.

C. Wellness Unit – under the command of the administrative Sergeant, develops, evaluates and implements department-wide training and resources on the various aspects of officer and civilian employee wellness.

a. The Return to Work Coordinator serves as a liaison between officers and the City of Fort Worth Department of Risk Management and the Medical Records Unit, is the primary police contact for questions regarding department policies and procedures pertaining to workers’ compensation, and conducts regular checkpoint contacts of injured/ill officers in order to provide support and assistance throughout their recovery and return-to-work process.

a. The Peer Support Coordinator, under the supervision of the Wellness Unit, may be requested by the command staff to provide assistance to an officer or employee who is undergoing a disciplinary action, to determine if there are underlying issues that need to be addressed outside the scope of discipline.

b. The Peer Support Team, which is under the supervision of the Wellness Unit and the Police Department Peer Support Coordinator, provides assistance for officers and civilian employees of the department with early intervention, preventive education, and assistance in any necessary referral.

Checkpoint members, under the supervision of the Wellness Unit, contact employees who have experienced critical incidents, traumatic events, or hardships to provide support, and possibly refer to peer support or professional services.

a. The Fitness Coordinator, which is under the supervision of the Wellness Unit, develops, evaluates, and oversees all fitness training programs for civil-service testing and police recruit training, oversees and reports compliance for annual department-wide fitness testing, develops fitness and nutrition programs, and other related training opportunities for police department employees.
